items: Push: add an item to the top. In Python a list is used as the stack and append() pushes.
Pop: remove the item from the top with the list's pop().

blocks.title: Python code (each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
stack_of_books = []
stack_of_books.append("Book A")
stack_of_books.append("Book B")
stack_of_books.append("Book C")
print("Stack:", stack_of_books)        # Book A, Book B, Book C
top_book = stack_of_books.pop()
print("Removed book:", top_book)       # Book C
print("Stack now:", stack_of_books)    # Book A, Book B
Like a stack of books on a desk, you can only add a book on top or take the top book off. Stacks are also used in depth-first search (DFS) to manage the nodes to explore in LIFO order (Did You Know).
